title: AI Associate
jobDescription:
We are looking for a hands-on AI Engineer with strong Python backend skills (FastAPI preferred) and practical experience in building AI-powered applications. This is not a research-only role. The candidate should be capable of developing AI models and integrating them into production-ready backend systems.
The ideal candidate should have built at least one AI-based solution for a real-world use case and should be comfortable working with modern AI tools, APIs, and backend architecture.
Key Responsibilities:
  • Design, train, test, and optimize AI/ML models for real-world business use cases.
  • Work on AI domains such as NLP, LLM-based systems, predictive analytics, or computer vision.
  • Build and maintain scalable REST APIs using FastAPI.
  • Integrate LLM services such as OpenAI or Hugging Face models into backend systems.
  • Implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines where required.
  • Handle data preprocessing, feature engineering, and model evaluation.
  • Work with databases such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQLite.
  • Manage API integrations, webhooks, background tasks, and asynchronous operations.
  • Document project architecture, workflows, and results clearly.
  • Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and brainstorming sessions.
Must-Have Skills:
  • Strong proficiency in Python.
  • Experience with FastAPI for building backend APIs.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one ML framework such as Scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.
  • Experience building at least one AI model for a defined use case (e.g., chatbot, text classification, image recognition, predictive model, AI automation tool).
  • Understanding of AI/ML concepts including data preprocessing, model evaluation metrics, overfitting and underfitting.
  • Experience working with APIs and JSON-based systems.
  • Familiarity with modern AI tools and frameworks such as GPT, Hugging Face, LangChain, or similar ecosystems.
Good to Have:
  • Experience with vector databases such as FAISS or Pinecone.
  • Understanding of RAG architecture and prompt engineering.
  • Basic knowledge of Docker and deployment processes.
  • Experience deploying AI models or backend systems to production environments.
Preferred Traits:
  • Self-driven and eager to learn emerging AI technologies.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical thinking ability.
  • Ability to write clean, maintainable, and well-structured code.
  • Effective communication and teamwork skills.

title: Technical Executive
jobDescription:
Technical Executive Position Overview
We are seeking a skilled Technical Executive with comprehensive floor-level knowledge of building systems to oversee day-to-day technical operations and maintenance activities. This hands-on role requires practical expertise in HVAC, UPS systems, and other critical building infrastructure.
Key Responsibilities
Technical Operations Maintenance
  • Supervise and coordinate daily operations of HVAC systems, UPS, DG sets, electrical panels, plumbing, and fire safety systems
  • Conduct regular inspections of all building systems and equipment to ensure optimal performance
  • Perform troubleshooting and coordinate corrective maintenance activities
  • Monitor energy consumption patterns and identify opportunities for efficiency improvements
  • Maintain accurate records of equipment performance, maintenance schedules, and service history
Vendor Contractor Management
  • Coordinate with external vendors and contractors for specialized maintenance and repair work
  • Supervise contractor activities to ensure quality standards and safety compliance
  • Review and verify contractor invoices and service reports
  • Manage spare parts inventory and coordinate timely procurement
Compliance Safety
  • Ensure all building systems operate in compliance with statutory requirements and safety standards
  • Conduct regular safety audits and implement corrective actions
  • Maintain updated documentation including equipment manuals, test certificates, and compliance records
  • Coordinate periodic inspections by regulatory authorities
Reporting Documentation
  • Prepare daily, weekly, and monthly technical reports on system performance and maintenance activities
  • Document equipment breakdowns, root cause analysis, and corrective actions taken
  • Maintain comprehensive asset registers and maintenance logs
  • Escalate critical issues to facility management promptly
Required Qualifications
Education Experience
  • Diploma or Bachelors degree in Mechanical/Electrical Engineering or related technical field
  • 3-5 years of hands-on experience in building operations and maintenance
  • Direct floor-level experience with HVAC systems (chillers, AHUs, FCUs, VRV/VRF systems)
  • Working knowledge of UPS systems, DG sets, electrical distribution, and switchgear
Technical Skills
  • Strong understanding of HVAC principles, refrigeration cycles, and air conditioning systems
  • Knowledge of UPS operation, battery management, and power backup systems
  • Familiarity with BMS (Building Management Systems) and monitoring platforms
  • Basic electrical troubleshooting and safety practices
  • Understanding of plumbing, fire fighting, and fire alarm systems
Key Competencies
  • Hands-on problem-solving approach with strong technical aptitude
  • Ability to work under pressure and handle emergency situations
  • Good coordination and communication skills
  • Attention to detail in documentation and reporting
  • Willingness to work in shifts and respond to after-hours emergencies
Working Conditions
  • Site-based role requiring regular floor presence and equipment inspections
  • May require working during weekends, holidays, or after hours for critical maintenance
  • Physical ability to access equipment rooms, rooftops, and confined spaces
  • Exposure to mechanical equipment, electrical panels, and varying environmental conditions
Preferred Qualifications
  • Certification in HVAC systems, electrical safety, or building operations
  • Experience with energy management and sustainability initiatives
  • Knowledge of facility management software and CMMS platforms
  • Previous experience in commercial real estate, corporate facilities, or industrial settings

jobDescription:

descriptionFromApi:
About the Role
Auric AI Labs is developing the worlds most advanced AI-powered vision intelligence platform for defense applications. We are building an AI-native intelligence system from scratch. No legacy DSP pipeline, no AI-as-classifier-stage, no hybrid compromises. We need an engineer to build the deep learning models that detect, classify, geolocate, and fingerprint radar and communications emitters directly from raw IQ data.
Why this role exists
Most AI in SIGINT today is AI bolted onto a 1990s DSP pipeline as a final classification stage. Filter, threshold, extract feature, then hand the leftovers to a small neural network. Each stage before the network throws away information the network could have used. Each hand-crafted feature is a prior the model is forced to inherit.
We are not doing that.
We are betting that an AI-native architecture, where deep learning operates on raw IQ data with minimal pre-processing, learns its own features, and replaces the deterministic stack rather than supplementing it, delivers a 5-10x improvement on every metric that matters: detection in low SNR, classification of unknown waveforms, specific emitter ID, real-time anomaly detection, cognitive EW.
This is not an AI feature inside a conventional product. The model is the product.
The actual problems
  • The signals are designed to defeat you: A modern LPI radar deliberately spreads its energy below the noise floor. A frequency-agile emitter changes frequency every pulse. Your job is to find structure that has been deliberately hidden.
  • You will not have real training data: Zero, for the signals that matter most. Before you can train a model, you have to answer a harder question: what does it mean for a model trained entirely in simulation to be trustworthy in the real worldYou will design the synthetic data pipeline, the channel models, the validation methodology, and the test for knowing when your simulator is wrong.
  • Every emitter is unique: Two radars of the same model number have hardware differences (oscillator drift, amplifier non-linearities, timing jitter) that fingerprint them individually. The problem is not which class of radar, it is have I seen this specific transmitter before, even in a different mode, even years ago. Open-set, fine-grained, unlabelled.
  • The DSP world will tell you it cannot be done: Some of their reasons are right. You will need to engage with them honestly, then figure out which ones are wrong and why.
Who we are looking for
Not a list of traits, those describe nothing. Specific, observable things we will recognise when we see them:
  • AI-native instinct: Your first instinct on a new problem is not what filter, transform, or heuristic applies here but what should a learned function take in, what should it output, and what is the right inductive bias. You think in terms of data, loss, and architecture the way a DSP engineer thinks in filter coefficients. You see hand-engineered features as priors to be questioned, not assumed.
  • You reason about whether a model fits its data: Not just whether it trains. You can look at a problem and argue, before writing code, why a particular architecture is or is not suited to the structure of the data it will see. You know that complex-valued signals, long-range temporal dependencies, and small distribution shifts each break specific assumptions, and you can name which.
  • You design experiments that can fail: Most ML work tunes until the loss goes down. Yours starts with the question: what result would prove I am wrong. You build the falsifying test before you build the model. With synthetic data and no real ground truth, this discipline is the entire difference between research that works and research that only seems to.
  • You read papers to find what the authors did not say: You reproduce a paper and notice the seed dependence the authors quietly omitted, the dataset preprocessing buried in the appendix, the hyperparameter that does most of the work. This habit is rare and it is what separates engineers who absorb a field from engineers who collect summaries of it.
  • The best work on your CV is work nobody assigned: A paper you reproduced because the result seemed too clean. A side project that became four months. An idea you kept thinking about after the class or job that introduced it had ended. The single hardest thing to fake.
  • You can turn a vague objective into a defensible ML problem: Detect this radar is not a specification. You can take an objective in plain English, decide what the inputs are, what the outputs should be, what the right loss is, and what evaluation would actually mean the system works in the field. This translation is most of the job.

About the Role
We are looking for a Data Analyst Executive to sit at the centre of how operations performs and
what it costs. From last-mile delivery and warehousing to fleet and vendor management, you will
build the reporting and analysis that tells us what is working, what is slipping, and where money
is leaking.
This is not a passive reporting role. You will own recurring dashboards, dig into performance
and cost deviations, and build the analysis that supports network, vendor, and process
decisions.
Key Responsibilities
Operational Performance Analytics
- Own daily and weekly dashboards across delivery performance, TAT/SLA adherence,
cancellations, and warehouse throughput.
- Investigate deviations - late dispatches, failed tasks, out-of-stock incidents, vehicle
idling - and identify root causes.
- Track productivity and utilisation across manpower, fleet, and warehouse capacity.
Cost Unit Economics
- Track cost per delivery, cost per trip, cost per item handled, and city-level cost-to-serve.
- Maintain month-on-month cost dashboards by city, cost head, and vendor with clear
variance commentary.
- Reconcile PO vs. GRN vs. invoice; audit vendor billing against rate cards and escalate
deviations.
- Identify cost leakages - idle capacity, empty return trips, excess deployment - and
size the savings.
Ops Strategy Projects
- Build business cases for network and vendor decisions: in-house vs. 3PL, fleet mix,
warehouse footprint, route restructuring.
- Support demand and capacity planning with volume trends and forecasting inputs.
- Run what-if analysis before rollout and measure impact after; support pilots and process
improvement projects end to end.
Automation Reporting Hygiene
- Automate recurring MIS using scripting or scheduled queries.
- Use AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, and similar) to speed up script writing, query building,
and data cleaning - with validation owned by you, not the tool.
- Maintain metric definitions and data quality checks so numbers stay consistent across
teams.
Stakeholder Management
- Partner with city ops, fleet, warehouse, procurement, and finance to align on definitions,
targets, and cut-offs.
- Present reviews to leadership in a decision-ready format - insight first, method second.
Must-Have Skills
- Advanced Excel / Google Sheets - can build a reporting workbook or cost model from
scratch.
- SQL - joins, aggregations, window functions, CTEs; comfortable with large
transactional tables.
- Analytical reasoning - can decompose a number into its drivers and explain what
actually moved.
- AI tools for analytics - uses ChatGPT, Claude, or similar to accelerate analysis, and
validates every output before it reaches a report.
- Business sense - connects a metric to the operational decision behind it.
- Ownership and detail - reconciles before publishing; treats an unexplained variance
as their problem to close.
Good-to-Have Skills
- Google Apps Script (or equivalent) for report automation and trigger-based workflows.
- MongoDB aggregation pipelines and Metabase or a similar query/dashboard layer.
- Exposure to procurement / P2P flows - PO, GRN, invoicing, cost heads.
- Prior experience in logistics, e-commerce, supply chain, or rental/subscription
operations.
Qualifications
- Bachelors degree in Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Commerce, or a
related quantitative field.
- 0-3 years in data analytics, MIS, business analysis, or operations strategy.
- Freshers with strong SQL and spreadsheet skills are encouraged to apply.
Why Join Us
- Direct line of sight into how operational decisions get made; your analysis reaches
decision-makers the same week.
- Autonomy to build the reporting stack from first principles.
- Steep learning curve across supply chain, fleet, warehousing, procurement, and
commercial negotiation.

We are looking for a driven and technically grounded developer with 1-2 years of hands-on experience to join our AI/ML & Generative AI team. This role is suited for professionals who have moved beyond entry-level exposure and are ready to take ownership of AI/ML pipelines, contribute to real-world deployments, and grow into a senior AI engineer role. You will work on machine learning, deep learning, large language models (LLMs), and generative AI systems including GPT models, Transformers, diffusion models, and more.

Core AI/ML Knowledge Required Machine Learning Fundamentals
  • Supervised, unsupervised, and semi-supervised learning paradigms
  • Classical ML algorithms: Linear/Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forests, SVMs, Gradient Boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM)
  • Model evaluation: cross-validation, bias-variance tradeoff, precision/recall, ROC-AUC
  • Feature engineering, data preprocessing pipelines, and handling imbalanced datasets
  • Hands-on experience with scikit-learn, NumPy, Pandas
Deep Learning & Neural Networks
  • Solid understanding of feedforward networks, backpropagation, and optimization (Adam, SGD, learning rate schedulers)
  • Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image/vision tasks
  • Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), LSTMs, and GRUs for sequential data
  • Attention mechanisms and how they led to the Transformer architecture
  • Experience with PyTorch and/or TensorFlow/Keras for model training and fine-tuning
Transformers & Large Language Models
Transformers are the backbone of modern AI. Candidates must have strong knowledge of:
  • Transformer Architecture Self-attention, multi-head attention, positional encoding, encoder-decoder structure
  • BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) masked language modeling, fine-tuning for classification, NER, QA
  • GPT Models (GPT-2, GPT-3, GPT-3.5, GPT-4) causal language modeling, prompt engineering, in-context learning, and API integration
  • T5, FLAN-T5 encoder-decoder models for text-to-text tasks like summarization, translation, and QA
  • LLaMA, Mistral, Falcon open-source LLM architectures, weight loading, and inference optimization
  • Hugging Face Transformers library model loading, tokenization, pipelines, and Trainer API
  • Tokenization strategies BPE, WordPiece, SentencePiece
  • Positional encodings absolute, relative (ALiBi, RoPE)
Generative AI Systems
  • Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) basics of generator-discriminator training
  • Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) latent space, reconstruction loss, KL divergence
  • Diffusion Models forward/reverse diffusion, DDPM, Stable Diffusion, ControlNet
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) vector retrieval, chunking strategies, reranking
  • Prompt engineering techniques zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, ReAct
  • Fine-tuning strategies full fine-tuning, LoRA, QLoRA, instruction tuning, RLHF basics
NLP Fundamentals
  • Text preprocessing tokenization, lemmatization, stopword removal, vectorization (TF-IDF, embeddings)

  • Word embeddings Word2Vec, GloVe, FastText, and contextual embeddings from Transformers
  • Semantic similarity, question answering, and dialogue systems

  • Conduct model evaluation, benchmarking, error analysis, and iterative performance tuning
  • Explore and implement reinforcement learning techniques (RLHF, reward modeling) to improve model interactions

  • Proficiency with Git, Jupyter Notebooks, and Linux command-line tools
Nice to Have (Not Mandatory)
  • Familiarity with MLOps tools: Weights & Biases, MLflow, DVC, or TensorBoard

descriptionFromApi:
Research Analyst Government Advisory


About Amber & Mark

At Amber & Mark, we partner with Governments and Public Institutions to turn ambition into outcomes bringing the rigour of strategy, the discipline of delivery, and an enduring belief in public purpose to every engagement. Our teams work closely with government departments, public agencies, and development institutions to advance governance transformation, institutional strengthening, and development impact.


Position Details

Position Title: Analyst Government Advisory

Area of Responsibility: Research

Number of Positions: 01

Location: Jaipur, Rajasthan

Reporting To: Engagement Manager

Employment Type: Full-time

Experience Required: 1-3 Years


Role Overview

Research Analyst Government Advisory supports the firm’s advisory engagements through research, document drafting, and proposal development across sectors. The role is research and document intensive - preparing proposals, detailed project reports (DPRs), concept notes, presentations, and research outputs — and requires strong analytical thinking, structured writing, and attention to detail. The Analyst works across assignments and sectors, translating research and inputs into clear, high-quality documents for internal teams and government and institutional stakeholders.

To support evidence-based policy formulation and Government decision-making through structured research, analytical insights, benchmarking, and preparation of high-quality advisory documents


Key Responsibilities

  • Conduct Policy research & analysis — Undertake secondary research on sectors, policies, schemes, tenders, and emerging trends to support advisory assignments. To Conduct comparative policy analysis, sector benchmarking, and best-practice research to support Government reforms, strategic initiatives, and advisory engagements
  • Data analysis & insight generation — Analyse qualitative and quantitative data from multiple sources, synthesize key findings, and develop actionable insights to support policy recommendations and project deliverables
  • Draft documents & notes — Prepare concept notes, briefing notes, background notes, executive summaries, and reports with clarity and accuracy.
  • Support proposal development — Assist in preparing proposals, bids, EOIs, and RFP responses, coordinating inputs from internal teams and domain experts.
  • Prepare DPRs & project documents — Support preparation of detailed project reports (DPRs), feasibility inputs, and project documentation.
  • Build presentations — Develop structured presentations, briefing decks, and visual summaries for internal and external audiences.
  • Track opportunities & tenders — Monitor tenders, EOIs, policy developments, and market opportunities relevant to the firm.
  • Prepare intelligence & sector briefs — Compile intelligence briefs, sector analyses, and insight notes to support advisory work.
  • Support documentation & knowledge management — Maintain proposal repositories, credentials, project sheets, trackers, and knowledge assets.
  • Coordinate & follow up — Coordinate with internal teams and stakeholders and ensure timely follow-up on inputs and deliverables.
  • Additional responsibilities — Undertake other research and documentation tasks assigned in line with organisational priorities.

Skills & Competencies

  • Research & analytical capability — Ability to conduct structured research and synthesise information into clear insights.
  • Data analysis & insight generation — Analyse qualitative and quantitative data from multiple sources, synthesize key findings, and develop actionable insights to support policy recommendations & project deliverables
  • Document drafting & writing — Strong ability to draft clear, concise notes, reports, and DPRs.
  • Proposal & business writing — Ability to prepare proposals, EOIs, and client-facing documents.
  • Presentation development — Ability to build structured, compelling presentations and briefing decks.

Underpinned by ownership, adaptability, and professional conduct across diverse assignments and sectors.


Qualifications & Experience

  • Education — Bachelor’s degree in Management, Economics, Commerce, Public Policy, Engineering, Political Science, Development Studies, Law, Liberal Arts, or a related discipline.
  • Preferred — Master’s / MBA / PGDM in Management, Public Policy, Economics, Development Studies, or a related field.
  • Experience — 1–3 years of experience in research, proposal development, documentation, consulting, or advisory, with demonstrated writing and analytical ability. Internship or project exposure to proposals, DPRs, or research is an added advantage. Experience in working with Private & Govt organisation, experience in deploying projects related to Government will be preferred.

Tools & Technical Proficiency

Mandatory: MS Word (Advanced), PowerPoint, Excel (Advanced), Google Workspace, and AI productivity / documentation tools.

Desired: Power BI / Tableau, Notion / ClickUp / Asana, online research databases, and workflow-automation tools.


Additional Information

  • Travel & mobility: willingness to travel within Rajasthan and other locations for field visits and stakeholder consultations.
  • Equal opportunity: Amber & Mark welcomes applications from candidates across all backgrounds.
  • Background checks: shortlisted candidates may undergo background and reference verification.
  • To apply: email your CV to careers@amberandmark.com with subject line as “Application_ (Position Title)”
